title: As-asked tidy (B): one issue access and one read per dispatch for the seal and plan read
description:
## As asked

Piece **B** of LIN-4354 ("LIN-4345 tidy-after: one home for each rule around the As-asked block"). The parent's scope, John's rulings and the full approved plan (revision 2) are in LIN-4354's description under `## Implementation Plan`, decision 4. Its approving review is comment `ccfeb340-79d8-4512-980e-451a194088df`, and that review's builder notes 1 and 4–6 apply to this piece. Repository: `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour).

**Starting point.** The parent's approved plan is where this piece starts. Read it in full in LIN-4354's description. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4354.

## This piece's slice of the approved plan

**One issue access and one issue read per dispatch.** This covers the seal and the file-pointer plan read.

**The factory's parameter**

* `createDispatchItem` (`lib/dispatch-factory.js`) takes one parameter, `issueAccess`: the lane's resolver of `{ provider, token }` or null. It replaces `readPlanBlock` and `sealAccess`.
* Migrate every lane: `dispatch-entrance.js:520-545, 1400, 1496, 1651, 1811, 1964` and `workspace-api-feedback.js:268, 336`.
* Delete `issueAccessOf`, `proxyAccess`, `planBlockOf` and `sealAccessFrom`. `SEAL_NO_ACCESS` becomes private to the factory.

**Provider I/O stays in** `lib/as-asked-seal.js` (review note 1). Keep two small functions there that take `{ provider, token }`:

* **A raw issue read.** Read through `issueDescription` when the provider has it, otherwise use `fetchIssueContext().issue`. A provider with neither counts as no access. Keep `trashed` in the result.
* **The description write.** Keep `updateIssue`, `normalizeWritePayload`, and writing by the issue ID the provider returned.

`as-asked-seal.js` also keeps `sealForFiling` and `providerHoldsAsAsked`.

**The factory owns the policy.** It decides when there is no access, and it caches the **in-flight read** for `fields.issueIdentifier`. The seal (step 1.7) and the pilot plan read (step 7.6) share it.

* A lane can never seed the read with an issue it already holds. The seal must write back raw stored text.
* **A trashed issue** is not sealed and keeps today's log line ("issue read found nothing"). The plan read still takes its description.
* **Identifiers** (note 4). Before deleting each lane's captured-identifier closure, confirm that the lane's `row.issueIdentifier` equals the identifier its plan read uses today. Include the descent arm's `terminalIdentifier`.
* **A failed read** (note 5). Choose one of two policies, state it, and name it in the PR:
  * share the rejected or timed-out read, which removes today's separate plan-read retry (pilot-only);
  * or retry once after a rejection.

**The test token, on Linear only.**

* Export `isHermeticTestToken(token)` from `lib/should-mock-ai.js`, defined as `NODE_ENV === 'test' && token === 'test-token'`.
* Three callers use it: `credentialFor`'s `isTestMode` (`dispatch-entrance.js:967`), `shouldMockAi` (which keeps its `|| provider === 'local'` arm), and the factory.
* **Only the factory** adds `provider.name === 'linear'`. With that, no provider call is made, the plan read gets no paths, and the seal logs "seal skipped: no access". The comment points at `installTestTokenLinearTransport` (`routes/test.js:58`).
* `credentialFor` stays independent of provider.
* The other test-token copies (proxy-compute, task-chat, workspace-api-steps, workspace-api-audit) are out of scope.

**Other**

* `valueWithin` (`dispatch-factory.js:757`) wraps `settleWithin` (`:917`). `valueWithin` never rejects. `settleWithin` still tells an error from a timeout. `dispatch-entrance.js:1005` is unaffected.
* Keep `fetchIssueContext` on the session context, because `guardComposedRun` still uses it.
* Update `docs/architecture/source-map.md:204` (where `sealAccessFrom` was described) and any architecture references to the adapters.

**Pilot-only consequences the PR must name.** All of these apply only with `HARBOUR_FILE_POINTER_PILOT` on, which is off by default:

* the session plan read goes through the workspace's own provider, not Linear's client;
* the override arm's plan read becomes a provider read, not the issue it already held;
* GitHub and Jira plan reads see the raw stored body;
* on Linear with `test-token`, the override arm loses the plan paths it got from mock data (note 6);
* the failed-read policy chosen above.

## Testing (the plan's witnesses 3, 4, 4b, 4c and 7)

* **Witness 3.** A first dispatch with the pilot on, through a counting fake provider **with** `issueDescription`, makes exactly one issue read (two today). It reads the row's `fields.issueIdentifier` and yields the plan paths. The existing verbatim, Linear-escaped and returned-issue-ID write assertions stay.
* **Witness 4.** Linear provider, `'test-token'`, `NODE_ENV=test`, and a counting transport installed through `setLinearFetchImpl` (`lib/linear-fetch.js:189`). It makes zero transport calls, still enqueues, and logs "seal skipped: no access".
* **Witness 4b.** `tests/unit/as-asked-dispatch-seal.test.js` (LocalProvider) and the proxy and recommend arms of `tests/unit/file-pointer-routes.test.js` pass **with their tokens and assertions unchanged**. If you must change a token or drop an assertion to get green, the skip is too wide.
* **Witness 4c.** A trashed issue with a plan yields plan paths and is not sealed.
* **What changes in existing tests.** The seal suite's `sealAccessFrom` uses (`:42, :98, :209, :268, :296`) become `issueAccess` resolvers. The lane census regexes (`:493-500`) move to `issueAccess`. The file-pointer session test (`:150-180`) stays green but no longer exercises its injected `fetchIssueContext`, which is expected.
* **Witness 7.** `npm run test:unit` and `test:hermetic` are green, as are the As-asked and file-pointer suites. Existing tests change only in how they hand in access.

## Done when

A dispatch has one way to hold its issue access and makes one read, and that read serves both the seal and the plan read. The E2E test-token 401 is gone, on Linear only. The pilot consequences are named in the PR. The witnesses above pass.

Session fit: fits one session

Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4354's approving plan-review (comment ccfeb340-79d8-4512-980e-451a194088df, rev 2)

**Grounding commits:**

* `cdc324bc` (HEAD the plan was read and approved at; LIN-4353)
* `d81e13e7` (LIN-4352, which added the adapters)
* `fdd57fe9` (LIN-4351)

**Landing order:** independent of piece A. Piece C follows A and B. This piece touches the write path, so it lands on its own.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Implemented

Implemented as approved in [PR #2349](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2349>), squash-merged as `93a37ab6` and deployed on 2026-11-07. `createDispatchItem` takes one `issueAccess` resolver. One cached read of `fields.issueIdentifier` serves both the seal and the pilot plan read. `isHermeticTestToken` skips the seal on Linear only. Failed-read policy: share the rejected or timed-out read.

The one deviation is announced on LIN-4354: `tests/unit/file-pointer-factory.test.js` was touched, and only its access wiring changed.

The full history (grounding, the PR record, review and close-out) is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
**Beat 1 (grounding and witnesses), on branch `feat/lin-4361-one-issue-access-one-read` @ `88c751d5`.** No drift: main is still `cdc324bc`, and every file and line the ticket names still maps. #2348 is open and touches none of this piece's files.

Base: main @ cdc324bc (no commits on main since the plan was read). PR #2348 is open, not merged; it touches none of
piece B's files (dispatch-factory, as-asked-seal, dispatch-entrance, workspace-api-feedback, should-mock-ai, linear-fetch).
It still has to rebase on whichever lands second.

## Identifier check (review note 4)
| Lane | Where | Plan read's identifier today | row.issueIdentifier → fields.issueIdentifier | Match |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| session | dispatch-entrance.js:1400 | `issueIdentifier` from `body` (sessionPlanRead) | `row: { ...body }` → body.issueIdentifier | yes |
| proxy | :1496 | `issueIdentifier` from `body` | `row: { ...body }` → body.issueIdentifier | yes |
| recommend override | :1651 | the held `issue`, resolved by `contextFor(…, body.issueIdentifier)` | `issueIdentifier` (body) | yes |
| recommend descent | :1811 | `terminalIdentifier` | `issueIdentifier: terminalIdentifier` | yes |
| kickoff | :1964 | no plan read (seal only, already factory-keyed) | `issueIdentifier` | n/a |
| feedback triage | workspace-api-feedback.js:268 | no plan read (seal only, already factory-keyed) | `fields.issueIdentifier: issue.identifier` | n/a |
| feedback autopilot | :336 | no plan read (seal only, already factory-keyed) | `issue.identifier` | n/a |
ROW_FIELDS.issueIdentifier is `r.issueIdentifier || null`; the pilot only runs with a truthy fields.issueIdentifier.

## Failed-read policy (review note 5)
Share the rejected or timed-out read. One cached in-flight promise per dispatch; a rejection or a timeout gives the plan
read no paths, which removes today's separate pilot-only plan-read retry. Reason: it is the simpler of the two, it is
literally "one read", and the pilot is fail-open already (`valueWithin`), so a retry would add a second read path to save
a pointer the pilot is built to do without. A read that timed out at the seal but settles before the plan cap still
serves the plan read, because the promise, not the seal's verdict, is cached.

## Today's behaviour, measured (scratch script through today's issueAccessOf wiring)
- w3: reads = [issueDescription FAKE-7, fetchIssueContext FAKE-7] (two), pointer delivered.
- w4: Linear + test-token: 2 transport calls, `seal failed: issue read failed (Authentication required…)`, enqueued, no pointer.
- w4c: trashed + plan: `seal failed: issue read found nothing`, pointer delivered, two reads.

**PR opened: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2349** (head `ee269337`, branch `feat/lin-4361-one-issue-access-one-read`). Not merged; it waits for review.

- `createDispatchItem` takes one `issueAccess` resolver in place of `readPlanBlock` and `sealAccess`. The factory resolves access once and reads `fields.issueIdentifier` once, and that read serves both the seal (step 1.7) and the pilot plan read (step 7.6).
- Provider I/O stays in `lib/as-asked-seal.js` (`readsIssues`, `readIssueRaw`, `writeIssueDescription`). `isHermeticTestToken` lives in `lib/should-mock-ai.js` and has three callers; only the factory adds the Linear-only skip.
- Failed-read policy: **share the rejected or timed-out read** (removes the pilot-only plan-read retry).
- The PR names six pilot-only consequences, all with `HARBOUR_FILE_POINTER_PILOT` on (off by default): the session plan read goes through the workspace's own provider; the override arm's plan read is a provider read; GitHub and Jira see the raw body; Linear `test-token` loses the override arm's mock plan paths; the failed-read policy; and a provider with only `issueDescription` now gets plan paths (no shipped provider is affected).
- Locally: `test:unit` and `test:hermetic` 24,119/24,119; witnesses 3, 4, 4b and 4c green; 10 of 10 mutations caught. CI run: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42397128070
- **#2348 is still open and must rebase** on whichever lands second. It shares no files with this PR.

CI is green on PR #2349 at head `ee269337`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan and `ci-success` all passed. Run: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42397128070. The PR is ready for review.

## Review — LIN-4361

Reviewed head `ee269337` on [PR #2349](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2349) (`feat/lin-4361-one-issue-access-one-read`), against base `cdc324bc`. Nothing has landed on main since the ticket was filed (2026-11-07T17:12Z), so the plan's file and line references still hold.

CI: green at `ee269337`. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and `ci-success` passed ([run 42397128070](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42397128070)). I also re-ran the suites myself: `test:unit` 24,119/24,119 and `test:hermetic` 24,119/24,119 with zero non-loopback sockets. Base `test:unit` gave 24,112/24,112. Neither side had any failures, so no failure names differ.

### Against what was asked
- **One parameter.** `createDispatchItem` takes `issueAccess`, and `readPlanBlock` and `sealAccess` are gone. All 7 lanes are migrated: session, proxy, override, descent, kickoff and the two feedback lanes. `issueAccessOf`, `proxyAccess`, `planBlockOf`, `sessionPlanRead`, `sealAccessFrom` and `SEAL_NO_ACCESS` are deleted, and grep finds none of them in `lib/`, `routes/`, `tests/` or `docs/`. `NO_ACCESS` is now private to the factory.
- **Provider I/O stays in `as-asked-seal.js`.** It holds `readsIssues`, `readIssueRaw` (`issueDescription`, falling back to `fetchIssueContext().issue`, with `trashed` kept) and `writeIssueDescription` (`updateIssue` plus `normalizeWritePayload`, by the returned id). `sealForFiling` and `providerHoldsAsAsked` are unchanged.
- **The factory owns the policy.** `resolveIssueAccess` decides when there is no access, and `dispatchIssue` caches the read promise while it is in flight. Lanes cannot seed it. A trashed issue is not sealed ("found nothing"), but its plan still yields paths.
- **Identifiers (note 4).** The comment table checks out against the code. Descent uses `terminalIdentifier` both for the row and in the old closure.
- **Failed-read policy (note 5).** "Share the rejected or timed-out read". It is stated in the PR and the code matches it: the promise is cached, not the seal's verdict.
- **Test token.** `isHermeticTestToken` has exactly three callers. `credentialFor` still ignores the provider, and `shouldMockAi` keeps its `local` arm. Only the factory adds `provider.name === 'linear'`, which matches `lib/providers/linear/index.js:2279`.
- `valueWithin` now wraps `settleWithin`, `fetchIssueContext` stays on the session context, and `source-map.md` is updated.
- **Pilot consequences.** The PR names all five required consequences and a sixth one: issueDescription-only providers now get plan paths.
- **Scope vs plan.** The implementation also touched `tests/unit/file-pointer-factory.test.js`, which the plan did not list. That deviation was announced on LIN-4354 (17:26Z). Only how access is handed in changed; no assertion lines changed. No other overrun.

### Done-when evidence
- **"The E2E test-token 401 is gone".** I checked the real E2E logs. Main's last CI run (42391774796) has **226** lines saying `seal failed: issue read failed (Authentication…`. This PR's run has **0** of them and 530 lines saying `seal skipped: no access`.
- **Witnesses 3, 4, 4b, 4c and 7** are all green. Witness 4b holds: `file-pointer-routes.test.js` is untouched, and no token or assertion changed in the seal suite (only how access is handed in, plus the census regex).

### Mutation check (I ran these in a separate worktree, each reverted, tree left clean)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Drop the read cache (`read ??=` → `read =`) | RED: witness 3 ×2, 4c |
| Remove the Linear test-token skip | RED: witness 4 |
| Skip test-token for every provider | RED: LocalProvider seal suite (4b guard) |
| Seal a trashed issue | RED: 4c ×2 |
| Plan read honours `trashed` | RED: 4c with plan |
| Write by identifier instead of the returned id | RED: id-keying tests |
| Prefer `fetchIssueContext` over `issueDescription` | RED: witness 3, id tests |
| Plan read ignores the shared issue | RED: witness 3, 4c |
| Each lane's `issueAccess` → `() => null` (session, proxy, override, descent, kickoff) | RED for every lane, through behavioural seal and pointer route tests, not only the source census |

### Regression check
`git log -30` on the touched files shows only LIN-4351/4352/4353 and earlier periodical and preamble work. Nothing was reverted, and no earlier fix is undone. LIN-4352's rule that "seal keyed by the row's issue (descent = terminal)" is still intact and pinned.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is **one dispatch reading its issue more than once.**
- `guardComposedRun`'s `fetchIssueContext` (terminal-anchor guard) is still a separate read. The As-asked block explicitly keeps it, so it is **outside**.
- The other `test-token` copies (proxy-compute, task-chat, workspace-api-steps, workspace-api-audit) are **outside**: As asked rules them out of scope.

No unhandled sibling sits inside this ticket's bounded class.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Pilot-on behaviour against real providers** (**inside**: the named pilot-only consequences 1–6). CI only exercises fakes and LocalProvider with `HARBOUR_FILE_POINTER_PILOT` on, and the pilot is off by default in production.
  - Settle by a **named monitor**: if the pilot is switched on, the `[file-pointer]` JSON log line (`delivered`, `failOpen`, `reason`) on implementation dispatches. If `delivered:false`/`failOpen:true` goes up compared with before the merge, the shared read or the raw-body change is at fault. Nothing short of a live provider with the pilot on can show this.
  - **Named rollback**: revert the PR #2349 squash commit. There is no migration and no persisted shape change, so it is reversible.
- **First-dispatch seal on live Linear, GitHub and Jira through the new `issueAccess` path** (**inside**: this ticket rewires the write path). CI covers fakes and LocalProvider, and E2E only covers the test-token skip.
  - Settle **after the deploy** by checking prod logs for the first `[as-asked] sealed at first dispatch` on an externally filed ticket.
  - Also confirm that no `[as-asked] seal skipped: no access` appears for real-token lanes. In prod that line would mean `resolveIssueAccess` is too narrow, because `NODE_ENV` is not `test` there and so the test-token skip cannot fire.
  - Same named rollback as above.
- **The two-branch run is mine, on my machine.** It does not stand in for a clean environment, but CI also ran green at this head, so this is not a gap. Close-out should re-check CI on the exact commit it merges. If PR #2348 lands first, this PR must rebase and CI must be green again on the rebased head (they share no files).

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The work meets "A dispatch has one way to hold its issue access and makes one read, and that read serves both the seal and the plan read. The E2E test-token 401 is gone, on Linear only. The pilot consequences are named in the PR. The witnesses above pass." It does so without narrowing. Close-out has no code fixes to make, only the ledger above to discharge.

## Close-out — LIN-4361

**Merged:** [PR #2349](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2349), squash-merged as `93a37ab6`. The merge was pinned to the reviewed head `ee269337` with `--match-head-commit`. Main had not moved from `cdc324bc`, so no rebase was needed. #2348 is still open and is the one that rebases now (they share no files).

**Deployed:** Railway `harbour-cat` deployment `3c04ad16` reports SUCCESS at `93a37ab6`, and the harbour.cat footer shows `93a37ab6`. The server booted cleanly with no errors in the logs.

**Meets what was asked**, quoting review: it meets "A dispatch has one way to hold its issue access and makes one read, and that read serves both the seal and the plan read. The E2E test-token 401 is gone, on Linear only. The pilot consequences are named in the PR. The witnesses above pass." It does so without narrowing.

**Changes made at close-out:** none. Review asked for no code fixes, and nothing in the code changed after the approval.

**Final CI:** green on `ee269337` (Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success; [run 42397128070](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42397128070)). Green on main at `93a37ab6` ([run 42398472766](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42398472766)).

### Ledger
- **Pilot-on behaviour against real providers** (inside, pilot consequences 1–6). Settled by review's **named monitor**: the `[file-pointer]` JSON log line (`delivered`, `failOpen`, `reason`) on implementation dispatches, if `HARBOUR_FILE_POINTER_PILOT` is ever switched on (it is off in production). **Named rollback:** revert squash commit `93a37ab6`. There is no migration and no persisted-shape change.
- **Live first-dispatch seal on Linear, GitHub and Jira** (inside, a post-deploy check). **Not run.**
  - Why: it needs the first dispatch of a ticket filed directly in the provider, with a non-empty description and no `## As asked` block. Tickets filed through Harbour are sealed at create. No such dispatch reached the new deployment during close-out, and producing one would mean launching a real agent run.
  - Who can run it: an operator, after the next such dispatch. In the `harbour-cat` production logs, look for `[as-asked] sealed at first dispatch (<ws> <ID>)`, and check that no `[as-asked] seal skipped: no access` or `seal failed` line appears for a real-token lane.
  - What I did check: the new deployment's logs have no `seal skipped` or `seal failed` lines so far. The previous deployment's baseline was one `sealed at first dispatch` line (LIN-4354) and no skipped or failed lines.
  - The same record is on the PR ([comment](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2349#issuecomment-6711044193)).
- **Exact-head CI and rebase if #2348 lands first.** Settled: #2348 had not merged, main was still `cdc324bc`, and CI was green on the exact merged head (above).

### Related tickets
- **LIN-4359** (the first-dispatch seal skipping the test-token sentinel in e2e) is closed as Done, because this PR delivers its done-when. Test-token mode is skipped with its own `seal skipped: no access` line. The E2E run has 0 `seal failed` lines against 226 on main's earlier run. Witness 4 asserts zero transport calls.
- **LIN-2847** (the audit of duplicated test-mode code) is linked as related. It already covers the `test-token` copies that As asked ruled out of scope (proxy-compute, task-chat, workspace-api-steps, workspace-api-audit), so no new ticket was filed.
- `guardComposedRun`'s separate `fetchIssueContext` read was kept on purpose by As asked. It is not a defect, so nothing was filed.
- **LIN-4362** (piece C) is still blocked by LIN-4360 (piece A). This piece no longer blocks it.

**Follow-ups filed:** none. The ledger had no outside items.

## Autopilot run summary — LIN-4361 (stepper)

**Beats (one warm session, Opus 4.8):**
1. Ground, branch, write witnesses first — no drift at `cdc324bc`; identifier check matched on every lane; failed-read policy: share the rejected/timed-out read. 6 of 7 new witnesses failed on the old code (`88c751d5`).
2. Core change — `issueAccess` parameter, shared in-flight read, `isHermeticTestToken`, Linear-only skip in the factory. Witnesses 7/7 (`acfd7b0b`).
3. Migrate existing tests, census, docs — only the way access is handed in changed; 10 mutations each caught. Unit and hermetic 24,119/24,119 (`ee269337`).
4. Push, PR #2349, CI green (run 42397128070), pilot consequences and the #2348 rebase note named in the PR.

**Then (fresh sessions):** review — Approve, conditional (comment `3de83c1e`; 13 mutations caught; suites re-run on branch and main). Close-out — squash-merged as `93a37ab6`, main CI green (run 42398472766), deployed, LIN-4361 Done (comment `9cec2852`).

**Verified by me:** PR state MERGED at `93a37ab6`; main run success on that SHA; LIN-4361 state Done with the As-asked block intact.

**Left for an operator:** the live first-dispatch seal on real Linear/GitHub/Jira tokens was not run (needs a ticket filed directly in the provider). Check prod logs for `[as-asked] sealed at first dispatch` and no `seal skipped: no access` from a real-token lane. Rollback: revert `93a37ab6`. PR #2348 must now rebase (no shared files).
